newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio police boost firepower to match drug gangs.
newsitem.headline: Rio police boost firepower to match drug gangs.

text.p: Police, who complain that their standard issue .38-calibre revolvers are no match for heavily armed drug gangs, will be issued 9mm automatic pistols to boost their firepower, authorities said on Thursday.

"The police need more powerful weapons because drug traffickers are using more sophisticated guns everyday," an official at Rio de Janeiro state's Public Security Secretariat said. He said Brazil's armed forces would supply 28,000 9mm pistols for police who patrol Rio's streets and shantytowns, where most of the violence takes place.
Aside from being a more powerful handgun, the 9mm has a magazine clip that holds up to 17 rounds. Revolvers currently used by most of the city's police force hold only six rounds.
